[SOURCE id=issue:569:569-summary:84e873f1b910 kind=issue issue=569 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#569.txt]
Issue: 569
Summary: In OpENer current master branch, the real unconnected explicit-message path from `RegisterSession` through `SendRRData`/CPF to `SetAttributeSingle` reaches a settable attribute in the default build, but request-data length is not checked before `attribute->decode(...)` is invoked. A crafted request that passes path decoding triggers a server-side out-of-bounds read in the attribute decoder (`GetUintFromMessage` / `GetUsintFromMessage`), and ASan reports it as a stack-buffer-overflow read.
Reproduce: Run the provided Python 3 PoC against the default POSIX OpENer server on `127.0.0.1:44818`. The script opens a socket, sends `RegisterSession`, extracts the session id from the reply, then sends `SendRRData` containing a `SetAttributeSingle` CIP message (`0x10`) in a Null Address / Unconnected Data Item CPF. Use the built-in `tcpip13` target for TCP/IP interface instance 1 attribute 13, or `qos8` for QoS instance 1 attribute 8; the crafted path is padded with `path_size_words=235`. Expected result: ASan reports a `stack-buffer-overflow` read in `GetUintFromMessage` / `GetUsintFromMessage`, with the trace passing through `DecodeCipTcpIpInterfaceEncapsulationInactivityTimeout` and `SetAttributeSingle`.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:570:570-summary:0b4cbe808107 kind=issue issue=570 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#570.txt]
Issue: 570
Summary: A malformed `ForwardOpen` request can trigger a network-reachable out-of-bounds read in OpENer during connection-path parsing. In `ParseConnectionPath()`, the trailing Simple Data Segment length byte is trusted without checking that it still fits the remaining path budget, so `remaining_path` can underflow and `message` can be advanced past the request buffer. The next `GetPathSegmentType(message)` access then reads out of bounds and crashes the server. The reachable path shown is `HandleDataOnTcpSocket()` -> `HandleReceivedExplictTcpData()` -> `HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand()` -> `NotifyCommonPacketFormat()` -> `NotifyMessageRouter()` -> `NotifyClass()` -> `ForwardOpen()` -> `ForwardOpenRoutine()` -> `HandleNonNullNonMatchingForwardOpenRequest()` -> `ParseConnectionPath()` -> `GetPathSegmentType()`. `HandleNonNullNonMatchingForwardOpenRequest()` calls `ParseConnectionPath()` before any `open_connection_function` is called.
Reproduce: Run the provided Python 3 PoC against an OpENer server listening on `127.0.0.1:44818`. The script registers a session, wraps a CIP `ForwardOpen` request to Connection Manager class `0x06`, instance `1`, inside `SendRRData`, and sends it over TCP 44818. It supports `baseline` and `crash`; `baseline` uses the valid path `20 04 24 97 2C 96 2C 64`, while `crash` appends `80 FF` so the trailing Simple Data Segment claims `0xff` words with only one word left. Command: `python3 poc.py crash`. On the vulnerable server, `ParseConnectionPath()` underflows `remaining_path`, advances past the request buffer, and `GetPathSegmentType()` dereferences out of bounds and crashes the server.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:564:564-summary:6b535e1b37b6 kind=issue issue=564 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#564.txt]
Issue: 564
Summary: OpENer commit 76b95cf has an out-of-bounds read in Connection Manager handling of malformed CIP ForwardOpen/LargeForwardOpen requests. `ForwardOpenRoutine()` in `source/src/cip/cipconnectionmanager.c` calls `ConnectionObjectInitializeFromMessage()` before strict minimal-length validation, and that parser in `source/src/cip/cipconnectionobject.c` repeatedly uses `GetByteFromMessage()`, `GetUintFromMessage()`, and `GetUdintFromMessage()` in `source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c` without a remaining-readable-length parameter for per-read boundary checks. A valid ENIP frame carrying a malformed ForwardOpen or LargeForwardOpen with insufficient request data can therefore leave the input pointer at the end of the receive buffer and still make `GetByteFromMessage()` read past it. The supplied ASan run reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` / `READ of size 1` in `GetByteFromMessage`, reached via `ConnectionObjectInitializeFromMessage()` and `ForwardOpenRoutine()`, overflowing the stack `incoming_message` buffer and aborting. The document states the issue is remotely triggerable over network traffic without authentication.
Reproduce: Prerequisites: the provided Python 3 PoC and an AddressSanitizer-instrumented POSIX OpENer binary from commit 76b95cf. Use the PoC against its documented defaults (`--host 127.0.0.1 --port 44818 --timeout 1.5 --attempts 50 --interval-ms 50`) and select `--service forward-open` or `--service large-forward-open`. [SOURCE id=issue:572:572-summary:4cac5b77f97f kind=issue issue=572 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#572.txt]
Issue: 572
Summary: In OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf, the real TCP explicit-message path on port 44818 (`RegisterSession` / `SendRRData`) can reach `SetAttributeList()` with a default-registered, non-settable `kCipShortString` attribute: Identity class, instance 1, attribute 7 (`product_name`). For non-settable attributes, `SetAttributeList()` still advances over the attacker-supplied value, and for variable-length types it calls `GetCipDataTypeLength(attribute->type, message_router_request->data)` without validating remaining length. For `kCipShortString`, that leads to an unchecked 1-byte read via `GetSintFromMessage()`. With a long padded EPath positioning `message_router_request->data` at the end of the 512-byte stack receive buffer, ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read. The document states this is at minimum a remote unauthenticated denial of service in the default build.
Reproduce: Use OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf with the default Ethernet buffer size (`PC_OPENER_ETHERNET_BUFFER_SIZE=512`). Start the server, then run the provided Python 3 PoC in `crash` mode against TCP port 44818 (default host `127.0.0.1`, override with `OPENER_HOST`). The script first sends `RegisterSession`, then `SendRRData` carrying a CIP `SetAttributeList` request to Identity class 1, instance 1, attribute 7. In crash mode it builds a long padded EPath (`build_path(233)`) and sends `attr_count=1`, `attr=7`, with no short-string length byte following the attribute id. Expected result: ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read when `SetAttributeList()` skips the non-settable short string value.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:574:574-summary:ec096521bf63 kind=issue issue=574 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#574.txt]
Issue: 574
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit `76b95cf` misparses `ForwardOpen` connection paths in `ParseConnectionPath()`. `CipEpathGetLogicalValue()` advances the `message` pointer according to the actual logical-segment encoding width, but `ParseConnectionPath()` decrements `remaining_path` by a fixed 1 word for the class segment and by 1 or 2 words based on the decoded value for configuration-instance and connection-point segments, instead of the segment’s actual on-wire width. When small values such as class `0x04`, configuration instance `151`, and connection points `150` and `100` are intentionally encoded as 32-bit logical segments, the parser consumes more path words than it accounts for, so `message` can move past the end of the received TCP packet while `remaining_path` remains positive. The later configuration-data loop then calls `GetPathSegmentType(message)` on that out-of-bounds pointer, producing a reproducible stack-buffer-overflow read on the server’s TCP receive buffer via `RegisterSession -> SendRRData -> CPF -> Message Router -> ForwardOpen -> ParseConnectionPath`.
Reproduce: Prerequisite: a running OpENer server from v2.3/master up to commit `76b95cf` listening on TCP `44818`.
